policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV reads positively, 'thou hast increased their joy'; its mapped textual_variant note assigns 'thou didst not increase the joy' only to another reading, distinguishing and selecting the qere/base reading.

ASV's 'Of the increase of his government' does not distinguish the qere and ketiv spellings, and no mapped textual note is supplied; both readings remain compatible, with the documented qere/base fallback retained.
